newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian stocks rebound from two-month lows.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian stocks rebound from two-month lows.

text.p: Shares on the Jordanian stock exchange rebounded from two month lows at the end of weekly trade on Wednesday, rising 0.29 percent as bargain-hunters returned to the market, brokers said.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose 0.42 points to 146.76 points in trade worth 419,000 dinars ($592,000).
"It's only a slight recovery, but today it wasn't just floor traders doing business," said one broker. "Outside investors were in there too."
Another broker said there appeared to be more cash in the market, which had fallen on Tuesday to its lowest level since early September.
Jordan Ceramic Factories, rising 0.10 dinars to 6.10 dinars in trade worth 92,000 dinars, and International Tobacco gaining 0.04 dinars to 1.14 in turnover of 32,000 dinars, led Wednesday's recovery.
Overall 24 stocks rose, just six fell and nine traded but closed unchanged on the market, which has traded in a narrow two-point range for much of the last two months.

Turnover, blighted by domestic economic worries and fears that Jordan will continue to be blocked out of trade with the neighbouring West Bank and sanction-hit Iraq, has halved since September to around 500,000 dinars a day.
